landmarks.name: Two Lovers Point
landmarks.writeup: A scenic cliffside lookout offering panoramic views of Tumon Bay, tied to a local legend of star-crossed lovers.

landmarks.name: War in the Pacific National Historical Park
landmarks.writeup: A park preserving sites and artifacts from World War II battles that took place on Guam.

landmarks.name: Fort Nuestra Señora de la Soledad
landmarks.writeup: A historic Spanish fort built in the 18th century overlooking Umatac Bay.

cultural_events.name: Guam Liberation Day
cultural_events.writeup: Annual celebration on July 21 commemorating the liberation of Guam from Japanese occupation in 1944.

cultural_events.name: Chamorro Month
cultural_events.writeup: Observed in March, this month celebrates Chamorro culture through festivals, dances, and traditional crafts.

food_writeup: Guam's cuisine is a blend of indigenous Chamorro flavors with influences from Spanish, Filipino, and American cooking, featuring dishes like red rice, kelaguen, and barbequed meats.
brief_history: Guam was first settled by the Chamorro people over 4,000 years ago. It was colonized by Spain in the 17th century, ceded to the United States after the Spanish-American War in 1898, occupied by Japan during World War II, and liberated in 1944. It remains an unincorporated U.S. territory.

important_people.name: Madeleine Bordallo
important_people.description: Former Delegate to the U.S. House of Representatives

current_conflicts: Guam faces strategic military tensions due to its location in the Pacific, particularly concerning North Korean missile threats and regional security dynamics.
